desc: Designs x86-compatible server processors and DCU AI accelerators for data centres, sold mainly to Chinese cloud, telecom and government customers.
markets: Customers are Chinese data-centre and state-linked buyers; US export restrictions limit overseas sales. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Little overseas consumer or enterprise brand need, and US trade restrictions make a Western F1 partnership impractical; technology showcase value is minimal.

desc: Fabless chip designer making DDR5 memory interface chips, PCIe retimers and clocking products for servers and data centres.
markets: Sells memory-interface chips to global server memory module makers and cloud operators, with customers across Asia and the US. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Component supplier with B2B customers; an F1 tie-in for AI-server credibility is conceivable but it has little brand-marketing culture.

desc: Distributes and retails Nissan and other passenger and commercial vehicles with after-sales service across several Southeast Asian and Asia-Pacific markets.
markets: Operates distribution in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam and other Asia-Pacific markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Dealer-distributor with regional reach; F1 could support brand-partner launches in Southeast Asia, though marketing budgets are principal-led and modest.

desc: Produces and distributes refrigerated packaged foods such as cold cuts, cheese and yogurt under brands including Fud and San Rafael.
markets: Sells in Mexico, the United States, Spain, Portugal and other European markets, plus Latin America; Bar-S is its US meat brand.
rationale: Mexico City and Austin Grands put its Mexican and US consumers in front of F1 crowds, supporting brand building and retail hospitality.

desc: Vietnam's largest electronics and grocery retailer, running Thegioididong, Dien May Xanh and Bach Hoa Xanh store chains.
markets: Stores are almost entirely in Vietnam; it has previously tried an electronics chain in Cambodia. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Large domestic retailer that could use F1 for brand prestige and supplier hospitality, though a Vietnamese customer base limits international value.

desc: Chinese premium colour cosmetics brand sold through its own counters, online channels and department stores for makeup.
markets: Sales are concentrated in mainland China through counters and online stores. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Brand-led beauty company; F1 could reach affluent female fans, but its sales are domestic and an overseas launch is not confirmed.

desc: Chinese gold jewellery brand selling heritage-style, craft gold pieces through its own boutiques in premium malls.
markets: Boutiques in mainland China, with a first overseas store in Singapore opened in 2025 and Hong Kong presence.
rationale: Luxury-positioned brand opening overseas stores; F1 could introduce it to affluent Asian and Middle Eastern buyers at races in Singapore and elsewhere.

desc: Markets and distributes prescription and consumer pharmaceuticals in China, mainly cardiovascular, dermatology and ophthalmology products, many licensed from foreign partners.
markets: Sells in mainland China through hospital and pharmacy channels. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Prescription-drug marketer in a regulated sector with little consumer brand need; F1 relevance is weak beyond corporate hospitality.

desc: Makes sintered neodymium-iron-boron rare-earth permanent magnets used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, industrial motors and consumer electronics.
markets: Supplies carmakers and industrial customers in China and overseas; magnets go into EV traction motors and wind generators.
rationale: Magnet supplier to EV and motor makers; F1 could showcase electrification materials to automotive buyers, but it is an unseen component brand.

desc: Peruvian miner producing zinc, lead and silver concentrates from underground mines in the central Andes, sold to smelters worldwide.
markets: Mines are in Peru; concentrates are sold under contract to smelters and traders in Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Commodity miner with no consumer brand and a controlling parent; an F1 deal offers little commercial value.

desc: Builds and operates water treatment, wastewater and waste-to-energy plants, mainly under concession contracts with Chinese local governments.
markets: Operations are concentrated in China. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regulated municipal-service operator with no consumer brand; an F1 partnership is unlikely to have a commercial rationale.
